378YE Summer Solstice Announcements by t.d: Using the legal power to resupply armies granted by the Senate, the Quartermaster General approved four resupply announcements, each counting separately for the purposes of a Synod veto. After the solstice he provided 112 wains of mithril and weirwood: 49 to the Red Wind Corsairs, restoring fighting strength equal to 980 soldiers; 43 to the Strong Reeds, restoring 860; and 20 to the Drakes, restoring 400. The Fire of the South received no wains, because it was engaged by Thule forces in Sermersuaq at the time.

n.Thule: Thule forces in Sermersuaq kept the Fire of the South engaged, which meant the Freeborn army received none of the resupply allocated to it.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark is not named, but the Fire of the South went unresupplied because it was fighting Thule forces in the Wintermark-held territory of Sermersuaq.

t.Sermersuaq: The Fire of the South was engaged by Thule forces in Sermersuaq and so received no resupply wains, leaving it without reinforcement for that fight.

378YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: In Segura three Imperial armies retook the Iron Plains at a cost of nearly two thousand soldiers, though three Lasambrian armies, aided by eternal emissaries under a golden lion banner, remain. Over ten thousand Thule invaded Sermersuaq and were checked but not expelled. In Karsk the Thule held their regions with potent sorcery. In Therunin Imperial magic and the Granite Pillar helped push the Druj back into Reikos. In Holberg the Druj broke Holmauer's walls, killing over four thousand Imperials. Jotun raids on the Greensward continued, the Virtue Crusade was destroyed in Reikos, and Imperial fleets disrupted Grendel shipping off Spiral.

n.Dawn: Dawnish forces fought on the Iron Plains and set up an armed camp near the ruins of Anduz, while Dawnish soldiers were among the defenders driven back into upper Holberg.
n.Druj: The Druj were pushed out of Therunin back into Reikos, but they overran Holmauer, besieged the Imperials in Holfried and slaughtered or enslaved the Virtue Crusade.
n.Grendel: The Grendel held their dug-in lines at Screed, but Imperial fleets sank their supply ships from Dubhtraig and captured treasure ships, disrupting links between Apulian and the Broken Shore.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar turned Druj terror back on them in Therunin, the Valiant Pegasus held Fort Mezudan, and the Virtue Crusade that marched from camps in Casinea and Bastion was destroyed.
n.Jotun: The Jotun still ruled Mournwold and Liathaven, and despite their ceasefire with the Empire their raiders kept attacking the Greensward.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns and Quiet Step, joined by risen Navarr dead, helped drive the Druj from Therunin, while Navarr captains raided Grendel shipping off Spiral.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs and Eastern Sky reclaimed the Iron Plains for the Freeborn, Freeborn troops defended Holberg and Freeborn corsairs harried Grendel fleets, though the Senate had yet to decide who would take custody of Segura.
n.The League: Holberg's defences collapsed to the upper city and its citizens began thinking of fleeing to Sarvos, Temeschwar or Tassato, while a Temeschwari merchant-venturer's fleet raided Grendel shipping.
n.The Marches: Marcher troops were among Holberg's defenders, and in the Greensward the scarecrows of Overton and Greensward Abbey sheltered Marchers from continuing Jotun raids.
n.Thule: A Thule host under the white hound invaded Sermersuaq, while in Karsk over twenty thousand Thule used powerful sorcery to hold their regions without counter-attacking.
n.Urizen: Urizen sentinels manned Fort Mezudan and the Phoenix fleet prowled the Spiral coast, where looted Urizen goods were recaptured from Grendel ships; Morrow was named as a possible Druj target.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle and Golden Axe lost about a thousand soldiers in Karsk, gained no ground and were forced back to Nitrost and Kopvenost, though Imperial magic spared them worse losses.
n.Wintermark: Fresh from Varushka, the Green Shield and Fist of the Mountain met the Thule invasion of Sermersuaq, losing many Winterfolk but stopping the orcs from establishing themselves.

t.Bastion: The Virtue Crusade camped on Bastion's borders before marching to its doom, and the Druj were said to have routes by which they could threaten Bastion.
t.Casinea: Refugees from Reikos gathered in camps on the borders of Casinea before marching out as the ill-fated Virtue Crusade.
t.Holberg: Druj forces broke the walls of Holmauer and penned around fifteen thousand Imperial defenders inside upper Holberg, killing over four thousand and spreading panic among its citizens.
t.Karsk: Imperial and Thule forces fought to a bloody standstill across Karsk, with neither side gaining ground and rival ice citadels raised in its hills.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was noted as still labouring under Jotun rule.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow was named as one place the Druj might threaten after their retreat from Therunin.
t.Mournwold: The Jotun still held the Mournwold and kept raiding the Marcher redoubt of the Greensward, despite the ceasefire.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: part of the Thule army that invaded Sermersuaq marched out of western Otkodov.
t.Reikos: The defeated Druj armies fell back into Reikos, where Druj scouts also crushed the Virtue Crusade and enslaved its survivors.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: frightened Holbergers began wondering what the weather was like in sunny Sarvos.
t.Segura: The Battle of the Iron Plains returned Segura to the Empire, though three Lasambrian armies still held its outer regions against three Imperial armies.
t.Sermersuaq: Over ten thousand Thule invaded Sermersuaq, seizing mines and mana sites in the Silver Peaks and raiding deep into the territory, beginning a war for it.
t.Spiral: Land forces in Spiral stayed dug in around Screed while Imperial fleets disrupted Grendel shipping off its coast.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Holbergers considering flight wondered about rain-beaten Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Holbergers wondered about chilly Temeschwar, and a Temeschwari merchant-venturer's fleet joined the raids on Grendel shipping.
t.Therunin: Imperial magic and the combined Navarr and Highborn armies drove over ten thousand Druj out of Therunin and back into Reikos.

r.Holberg/Holfried: The Imperial armies retreated behind the walls of Holfried, the upper city, where they were besieged and bombarded with the remains of their dead.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Druj broke Holmauer's walls in three places and retook its ruined suburbs and outer walls.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: The Druj commanded the siege from their fortress at Rebeshof, from whose gates the Scorpion Sting launched the assault on Holmauer.
r.Karsk/Branoc: Most of the serious fighting in Karsk took place in Branoc's northern hills, beneath the Broken Barrow, held by a hostile host aiding neither side.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The Thule raised a citadel of ice and frozen stone in fallen Krevsaty, from which orc warlocks watched the battlefields.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: The Varushkan forces were pushed back to Nitrost after failing to dislodge the Thule.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Jotun raiders kept attacking the Greensward, held back only by the scarecrows of Overton, its militia and the warded Greensward Abbey.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: the Thule army that invaded Sermersuaq came partly out of Sküld.
r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Lasambrian forces escaped to Anduzjasse and held old Anduz, while Dawnish forces camped above the Longing Circle facing them.
r.Segura/Burnish: Burnish was one refuge for the retreating Lasambrian armies, which still remain in Segura.
r.Segura/Iron Plains: The Iron Plains were reclaimed for the Freeborn after a costly battle in which nearly two thousand Imperial soldiers fell.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Yellow Chase was one refuge for the retreating Lasambrian armies, which still remain in Segura.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Thule raiding parties were reported as far south as the East Floes above Wreck.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule occupied the northern passes of the Silver Peaks, claiming mines and Stonefields mana and scouting the Stonefield Ice Caves while Wintermark's armies fought them.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Imperial fleets blockaded Apulus's waters, sinking Grendel supply ships and capturing treasure ships, though some Imperial ships were said to trade at Apulian.
r.Spiral/Screed: Highborn and Urizen held Fort Mezudan in Screed, facing the dug-in Grendel Salt Dogs and Stone Gyre.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Shadow magic in the fens of the Lower Tarn Valley raised a castle of mist and enchanted the marsh against the Druj invaders.

Archive:378YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.d: The roll names every territory's senator and the Senate's other offices, including Gideon of the Suns of Couros as Conscience of the Senate and Sendero i Hazana i Guerra as Admiral. It lists the generals of every Imperial army, the Warmage Vaan of Auric Horizon, and the Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and other posts. It also gives the six Archmagi, the Grandmasters of the Orders, and the Bourse holders with their winning bids. The Regario Dossier was uncontrolled and due for election next festival. The Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund remained in Druj hands and would not be auctioned until those territories were Imperial again.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senators were Bohemond De Rondell (Astolat), Ywain De Gauvain (Semmerholm) and Valentin Ivarovich Orzel (Weirwater). It fielded three generals, and Agnetha De Rondell and Tancred De Rondell sat in the Synod as Cardinal of Wisdom and Gatekeeper of Loyalty.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are noted as holding the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund, which are withheld from auction.
n.Highguard: Highguard held three Senate seats and three generalships. It also held three cardinalships (Courage, Loyalty and Pride), the gatekeepers of Prosperity and Vigilance, and the Grandmastership of the Sevenfold Path.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs had General Bloodcrow Martok of the Winter Sun and General Braka of the Summer Storm. Irontide Bruc served as Advisor on Orc Affairs and Irontide Vio held the Steel Fist.
n.Navarr: Navarr's senators were Rhain, Syn Nighthaven and Caerwyn Summer Crow, with Carr Foxden and Gwai commanding the Black Thorns and Quiet Step. Meir Pathfinder led the Rod and Shield and Idris Eternal held the Thimble.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn held four Senate seats, two generalships and the office of Admiral. They also held the Grandmastership of the Golden Pyramid and the Broken Shore Bounty.
n.The League: Besides three senators and General Gabriel Barossa of the Wolves of War, Leaguers held the Quartermaster General's post, two cardinalships and several Conclave offices. The League's Regario Dossier was uncontrolled and due for election next festival.
n.The Marches: The Marches were represented by senators Orrick, Bridget Eastville and Henry Ward. Their three generals led the Drakes, the Strong Reeds and the Bounders.
n.Urizen: Urizen's senators were Lucius of Quicksilver Spire, Marissa Shatterspire and Cato, and Tanwyn Ankarien led the Citadel Guard. Solas served as High Exorcist and Livia Cascade as Gatekeeper of Wisdom.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four Senate seats and two generalships, and Varushkans served as Auditor of Senatorial Accountability and Imperial Inquisitor. They also held the Grandmastership of the Shuttered Lantern, the Deanship of the Lyceum and two national Bourse seats.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's four senators were Hengest Dun, Uskolli, Atte and Jorma Steelhail, with generals leading the Green Shield Army and the Fist of the Mountain. Wintermark held the Stonefield Ice Caves and the Brilliant Shore, and Aedred apMagor was envoy to the Sumaah Republic.

t.Astolat: Bohemond De Rondell held the Senate seat for Astolat.
t.Bastion: Jada of Ravensfell held the Senate seat for Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Orrick held the Senate seat for Bregasland, the Dour Fens.
t.Casinea: Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold held the Senate seat for Casinea.
t.Feroz: Kattalin i Hazama i Guerra held the Senate seat for Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun held the Senate seat for Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: Rhain held the Senate seat for Hercynia.
t.Holberg: The Great Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg were held by the Druj and would not be auctioned until Holberg was once again Imperial.
t.Kahraman: Rauul i Jannat i Requiza held the Senate seat for Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Uskolli held the Senate seat for Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Constantin held the Senate seat for Karov.
t.Karsk: Machek Winterborn held the Senate seat for Karsk.
t.Madruga: Sallur i Mnajdra i Guerra held the Senate seat for Madruga.
t.Miaren: Syn Nighthaven held the Senate seat for Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Radomir held the Senate seat for Miekarova.
t.Mitwold: Bridget Eastville held the Senate seat for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Lucius of Quicksilver Spire held the Senate seat for Morrow.
t.Necropolis: Adamah of the Silent Tide held the Senate seat for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Marissa Shatterspire held the Senate seat for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: The Great Forest at Reikos was held by the Druj and would not be auctioned until Reikos was once again Imperial.
t.Sarvos: Mirislav held the Senate seat for Sarvos.
t.Segura: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra held the Senate seat for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Ywain De Gauvain held the Senate seat for Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte held the Senate seat for Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Jorma Steelhail held the Senate seat for Skarsind.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato held the Senate seat for Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Drogon Morosini held the Senate seat for Temeschwar.
t.Therunin: Caerwyn Summer Crow held the Senate seat for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Henry Ward held the Senate seat for Upwold, the Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Vitomyr Krasiludovich Antonov held the Senate seat for Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Valentin Ivarovich Orzel held the Senate seat for Weirwater, and the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat was held by Niccolo dos Tassatos for 98 Thrones.
t.Zenith: Cato held the Senate seat for Zenith.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund remained in Druj hands and were withheld from the Bourse until Holberg returned to Imperial control.

Assignment of Segura.d: After a long military campaign, Segura was conquered and a motion was brought to assign it to the Brass Coast. The motion was proposed by the senator for Segura and seconded by the senator for Kahraman. As a result, Segura became part of the Brass Coast nation. The territory was noted to be far from secure, however: Lasambrian orcs still controlled three of its seven regions, and the loss of just one more region would mean the loss of Segura as an Imperial territory.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast gained Segura as a new territory, though its hold was precarious, with Lasambrian orcs still holding three of the seven regions.

t.Segura: Segura was formally assigned to the Brass Coast after its conquest, but it remained insecure, with Lasambrian orcs controlling three regions and the loss of one more threatening its Imperial status.

Construct conservatory for the Anvil Hos.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Tassato, the motion passed at a cost of 15 thrones and required 27 wains of weirwood, which Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato allocated in Autumn 378YE, with completion due by Winter 378YE. Once complete, the conservatory produces 10 doses of True Vervain and 5 each of Marrowort, Imperial Roseweald, Cerulean Mazzarine and Bladeroot every season. Its creation establishes Origen's Rest as an Imperial title appointed by the Senate. Although the motion intends the herbs to benefit the Anvil Hospital, the citizen holding the sinecure is free to use the bounty as they see fit.

n.Urizen: Urizen hosts the new conservatory, built on the herb garden of the retired speaker Origen, so Urizen land now produces herbs for the Senate-appointed title of Origen's Rest.

t.Zenith: The conservatory is built in Zenith, where it is due for completion by Winter 378YE and then produces herbs including True Vervain each season.

Construct fortified garrison in Overton.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Feroz, the motion sought funds to buy wains for a blockhouse in the Mourn, with a view to future upgrades. It passed at 15 Thrones. The garrison required 5 wains of white granite for a fortified manor house, to shelter local citizens, and 5 wains of weirwood for a staging house, so military units could base themselves in Overton to protect the citizenry. It carried 2 Thrones upkeep. Silas Merrick of the Marches supplied the granite in Summer 378YE and the weirwood in Autumn 378YE. At the Spring Equinox 380YE, after Orchard's Watch was completed, the Senate disbanded the garrison when it created the Sheriff of Overton title.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name the Jotun; the garrison was commissioned in Overton, in the Mournwold, which they held at the time.

t.Mournwold: Overton in the Mournwold was to gain a fortified manor house as a refuge for its citizens and a staging house where military units could be based to protect them. The garrison stood until it was disbanded in 380YE to create the Sheriff of Overton title.

Construct memorial at Anvil.d: Proposed by the Conscience of the Senate and seconded by the senator for Bastion, the motion called for a memorial to the fallen at Anvil. It passed in principle, but no funding was requested at the time. The listed cost was 3 wains of white granite for the monument alone, or 10 white granite for a monument that also served as a sinecure. After the Winter Solstice of 378YE, Ira of Felix's Watch Banner of Highguard provided 10 wains of white granite. Once complete and the title clarified, the sinecure will automatically create the title of Custodian of the Imperial War Memorial.

n.Highguard: Highguard had a hand in the memorial at both ends: Bastion's senator seconded the motion, and Ira of Felix's Watch Banner of Highguard later supplied the 10 wains of white granite needed to build it.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea, held by Highguard, is not named on the page; the memorial is to be built at Anvil, not in Casinea.

Construct museum.d: The senator for Bastion proposed the motion and the senator for Necropolis seconded it. It called for a museum to store and display Imperial relics and artefacts, to be rebuilt in Bastion after the loss of the Tabernacle museum in Reikos. The proposer offered to fund the work personally but asked the Senate and individual senators to contribute. The motion passed at a cost of 8 Thrones and 10 wains of white granite. Jada of Highguard supplied the granite after the Winter Solstice of 378YE. Once the work was complete, the title of Curator of the White City Museum was created.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but the motion followed the destruction of the Tabernacle museum in the fighting over Reikos, which was then in their hands.
n.Highguard: Highguard gained the Empire's replacement museum in its territory of Bastion, and Jada of Highguard supplied the white granite needed to build it. The work led to the creation of the Curator of the White City Museum title.

t.Bastion: Bastion's senator proposed the motion, and the new Imperial museum for relics and artefacts was built there, which led to the creation of the Curator of the White City Museum title.
t.Reikos: Reikos lost the Imperial museum at Tabernacle, destroyed in the fighting there, and the Empire chose to rebuild it in Bastion instead.

r.Reikos/Riverwatch: The museum in Tabernacle, in Riverwatch, was destroyed in the recent fighting, which prompted the motion to build its replacement in Bastion.

Disburse funds to Bregasland.d: Proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Mitwold, the Summer 378YE motion distributed funds to Bregasland with the intention of resupplying the armies, with the Quartermaster General called as an expert witness. The page records 200 Thrones disbursed to Orrick, Senator for Bregasland, that season. In Autumn 378YE a similar motion, proposed by Bregasland and seconded by Hahnmark, sought funds to resupply the Imperial armies either through future motions or the Imperial Quartermaster, and 400 Thrones were disbursed to Orrick.

n.The Marches: A Marcher senator, Orrick of Bregasland, received Imperial funds entrusted to him for resupplying the Empire's armies.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland's senator Orrick proposed the motion and was given 200 Thrones in Summer and 400 Thrones in Autumn 378YE to put towards resupplying the Imperial armies.

Establish contact with Barrens orcs.d: Independent orcs were believed to be living in the Barrens and fighting the Druj. The motion proposed using the Autumn ritual Call Winged Messenger, which can carry a letter to anyone whose name and physical location the caster knows, to contact them and invite a delegation to Anvil. The ritual is magnitude 6, and a coven that has mastered it can cast it for 3 crystal mana. The motion passed in principle, but no funding was requested. Whether any messages were actually sent, and what came of the approach, is not recorded.

n.Druj: The motion sought to reach orcs who were believed to be fighting the Druj in the Barrens, a possible first step towards finding allies against them inside their own lands.

t.The Barrens: The motion targeted the unaligned orcs thought to live in the Druj-held Barrens, inviting them to send a delegation to Anvil, though whether contact was ever made is unknown.
